sections.markdown:
## C2 — KG hints for Pedestrian Safety, School Buses and Bicycle Safety

FACT_ID: sec17-R01 | anchor: A02
Traffic in the school bus's lane and all adjacent lanes must stop for flashing red lamps, while opposite-direction traffic on a divided highway is exempt [A02].
Why it matters: group_hint school-bus; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec17-F15 and sec17-F16.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec17-R02 | anchor: A01
A blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog must be given a stop regardless of the signal, while other pedestrians are owed a slowdown, readiness to stop and a horn warning as needed [A01].
Why it matters: group_hint driver-duties; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec17-F06 and sec17-F05.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec17-R03 | anchor: A03
A motorist passing a bicyclist should keep at least three feet of clearance until safely past, while opening a vehicle door unexpectedly in a way that creates a hazard for moving traffic or bicyclists is a traffic violation [A03].
Why it matters: group_hint three-feet; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec17-F21 and sec17-F32.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec17-R04 | anchor: A04
Bicycles ride at the right edge of a two-way road, while on a one-way road they may ride along the left edge [A04].
Why it matters: group_hint bicycle-position; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec17-F27 and sec17-F19.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec17-R05 | anchor: A04
Sidewalk riding is forbidden in business districts, while elsewhere it is allowed at ten miles per hour or less with pedestrians given the right of way [A04].
Why it matters: group_hint bicycle-rules; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec17-F30 and sec17-F28.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec17-R06 | anchor: A01
A pedestrian must cross only within crosswalks rather than jaywalking, while a pedestrian facing a green light that has been showing for some time should wait for the green signal on the next cycle before starting across [A01].
Why it matters: group_hint pedestrian-duties; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec17-F11 and sec17-F12.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec17-R07 | anchor: A03
Wrong-way riding causes about a quarter of bicycle and car crashes, while passing a bicyclist and then turning right across the rider is the crash named for motorists [A03].
Why it matters: group_hint bicycle-crashes; prereq_hint sec17-R03; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec17-F20 and sec17-F21.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec17-R08 | anchor: A01
Pedestrians make up twenty percent of Hawaii traffic deaths, while almost half of pedestrian deaths are people under fifteen or over sixty-five [A01].
Why it matters: group_hint statistics; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec17-F01 and sec17-F02.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec17-R09 | anchor: A02
A pedestrian walks on the left side facing traffic, while a bicyclist rides on the right side with traffic [A02].
Why it matters: group_hint position; prereq_hint sec17-R04; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec17-F13 and sec17-F25.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec17-R10 | anchor: A04
A bicyclist may turn left from the center of the lane like a car, while the pedestrian-style option is to walk the bicycle across in the crosswalk [A04].
Why it matters: group_hint bicycle-turns; prereq_hint sec17-R04; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec17-F35 and sec17-F32.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec17-R11 | anchor: A01
Driving through a pedestrian safety zone and passing a car stopped for a pedestrian are both prohibited by law, while sounding the horn to warn a pedestrian on the roadway is required by law [A01].
Why it matters: group_hint driver-duties; prereq_hint sec17-R02; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec17-F07 and sec17-F05.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec17-R12 | anchor: A04
A night-riding bicyclist must have a headlight and rear reflector, while a rear light, pedal reflectors and light clothing are only recommended [A04].
Why it matters: group_hint bicycle-rules; prereq_hint sec17-R05; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec17-F29 and sec17-F34.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0098]
